paragraphs.assessment: The two equations cancel one acetyl-CoA and acetoacetyl-CoA to give acetoacetate + CoA -> acetate + acetyl-CoA. Recycling is stated as material balance rather than enzyme channeling.

Native transfer L2R and native thiolase R2L agree with the selected Rhea oriented equations. Reversibility and explicit anion identities are preserved without counting the projections as extra reactions.

Both constituent equations and all eight sides agree with the complete native frames. Condensation orientation is explicit; the protein-bound residue classes do not specify free cysteine or experimental occupancy of AtoB Cys88.

Whole assembly components and reciprocal membership establish one alpha dimer plus one beta dimer and a separate AtoB tetramer. The draft does not transfer whole-complex catalysis to individual chains.
Apparent experimental masses and current sequence-derived properties remain separate. The old 2003 model assignments and current membrane-associated cytoplasmic annotation are accurately attributed.

Native intermediate and ping-pong discussion plus UniProt Km values are retained as database annotations of the inaccessible kinetic papers. The direction-specific values do not become a universal rate law.

All four complete Regulation frames support the source-qualified inhibitory relationships. The uncited acetyl-CoA frame is identified; exact assay concentrations are not invented. The mercurial InChI matches the anion.

The historical 200–300-fold induction statement occurs in native pathway/protein context. The draft correctly avoids assigning a freshly verified historical strain or denominator without the 1972 full paper.

The complete 1975 Methods distinguish oleate-grown wild-type B ATCC 11775 thiolase I from acetate-grown constitutive fadR16 fad-5 atoC49 thiolase II. The native broad B attribution is explicitly qualified.
The full 1975 assay recipe, 25 C conditions, substrate-concentration distinction, and below-1-percent C6 result are accurately bounded. Conditional non-detection does not become universal absence.

The indexed 2016 abstract and native BL21/sequence-match statements support the qualified structural account. The full 2016 article and exact cloning alignment are not claimed; the older mass remains separate.

Native kinetic slots carry distinct directions, units and references. The 470 micromolar BRENDA/1976 annotation is not silently reconciled with 138.6 micromolar/2016, and rates are not converted into flux.
AtoB 88/349/379, AtoA 46 and AtoD 24–30 are represented with their similarity or model evidence. Generic residue classes are not collapsed to a proven single protein site.
The two 1987 indexed abstracts distinguish structural-gene complementation from galK transcriptional regulation and preserve the historical atoDAB versus later atoDAEB nomenclature.
The complete 2007 promoter experiment supports the stated fragments, modified M9 glucose plus 10 mM acetoacetate and promoter-specific controls. This is expression regulation, not enzyme allostery.

The full 2007 study explicitly reports unsuccessful significant in-vitro phosphorylation of the His10 preparation. DNA binding and failure of added acetoacetate to improve it do not establish phosphorylation-independent physiological signaling.
The full footprint and promoter-mutation data support two 20-bp sites relative to a predicted start. The -53 binding/induction distinction and the predicted-coordinate limitation are retained.
The complete ChIP and IHF experiments use the stated BW25113/BW28878 and N99/N7193 contexts. Plasmid-promoter occupancy is not quantitative metabolic flux evidence.
The 2005 indexed abstract and complete native/UniProt objects retain D55G/H73L and phosphorylation ambiguity. The separate cPHB phenotypes are not relabeled as acetoacetate flux.
The full source contexts and indexed 1993/2006/2007/2011 abstracts support the bounded antizyme, cPHB and motility discussion; these are excluded from the core chemistry.
Both complete AtoC feature sets show the stated version-dependent HTH endpoints and the older sequence caution. Feature differences do not create a new wild-type allele.
The complete K-12 and O157:H7 entries plus indexed 2005 abstract keep the orthologs distinct. Catalytic capacity is not evidence for route-growth necessity.

The complete O157:H7 UniProt and native accounts support the broad substrates, conditional isovalerate negative and glutamyl-CoA intermediate. K-12 Glu333/tetramer inheritance remains similarity evidence.

The full 2022 Methods and Fig.2 show the reverse acetate assay, stated donor/acceptor concentrations, enzyme amount, temperature, time and LC–MS products. Forward acetoacetate assimilation is not claimed as directly measured.

The complete 2022 main article separates pET28a/BL21(lambdaDE3) protein production from MG1655 physiology. Protein-lactylation and PykF experiments do not become route steps; supplementary cloning details remain unverified.

All five PathBank reactions and 21 sides were inspected. The CoA-product/one-acetyl-CoA thiolase equation is incompatible and correctly rejected; the three other acetate-metabolism events remain outside the boundary. AtoB four-chain coefficient is explicit while AtoDA coefficients are absent.
Native acetyl-CoA/TCA interface supports the stated metabolic connection, without ATP yield or universal flux claims. Species indexing is separated from each experimental strain context.
Native engineering and nomenclature comments remain application/history context. Engineered butanol or medium-chain products do not replace the physiological acetoacetate endpoint.

Evidence-depth wording matches the acquired originals: three full main papers, indexed abstracts where available, otherwise metadata and attributed native annotations. No blanket full-paper or supplement-reading claim is made.
